messages:
zoe: Quick sync — following up on yesterday's spike comparing ephemeral NAT pools vs per-tenant static IPs. Wanted a quick check before writing RFC.
ravi: Short list of concerns please: cost, ops, and customer UX.
zoe: Sure. Option 1: Static per-tenant IP (current enterprise model). Pros: predictable ACLs, simple for customers. Cons: high reserved capacity cost, onboarding friction.
eldon: Option 2?
zoe: Option 2: Ephemeral NAT pool (tokenized allocations). Agent requests short-lived IP allocation from CP, CP maps tenant->IP in a per-region pool. Pros: lower reserved footprint, good for self-serve. Cons: CP load, mapping state, debugging complexity.
ravi: How short-lived? minutes or hours?
zoe: Configurable TTL. Default 15m, renew on demand. Longer leases for long-lived flows (e.g., >1h) with escalation.
eldon: Failure modes: what if CP is down and agent can't renew?
zoe: Fallback plan: 1) keep current allocation until TTL; 2) fallback to regional relay; 3) emergency direct egress (with warnings). Must be explicit in RFC.
inf-bot: infra:pool/warm-nat scaled to 12 nodes in eu-west-1 :signal_strength:
ravi: Operational notes: need cp-cli `egress allocations --tenant T` and audit events. Also rate-limit allocation attempts per tenant (prevent storm).
zoe: Security: signed short-lived pledges with nonces to prevent replay. All allocations logged to tenant audit.
eldon: Cloud limits: some clouds don't support fast ENI churn. Implement NAT pool with iptables mappings on warm hosts instead of ENI churn.
ravi: Agrees. Ask for cost estimates at 10k tenants and decision matrix in RFC.
zoe: Will write RFC with recommendation: ephemeral pool as default for self-serve, static IPs remain enterprise opt-in. Pilot plan included. Tagging you both when ready.
